extracted.intended_audience: authors submitting to ICML 2023 (machine learning researchers); reviewers asked to consider these guidelines
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and checklist for preparing ICML 2023 conference papers, covering ethics, reproducibility, data/assets, human subjects, theoretical and experimental reporting. Intended to guide authors (and inform reviewers) about required disclosures and best practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible ML focus
rubrics_metrics.description: Promote best practices for responsible machine learning research, including reproducibility, ethics, transparency, and impact on society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should check their paper and supplemental materials in the context of these guidelines; reviewers will be asked to consider them as a factor in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication ethics compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Have you read the publication ethics guidelines and ensured that your paper conforms to them?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure adherence to the conference's publication ethics (see linked policy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion of negative societal impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss any potential negative societal impacts (for example, disinformation, privacy, fairness) of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider direct paths to negative applications, stakeholders who may be harmed even if others benefit, and possible harms through intended use or misuse. The page references unofficial guidance and NeurIPS/FAccT resources for broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation and versioning of used assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If your work uses existing assets, did you cite the creators and the version?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite original creators and specify the exact version of datasets, code, or models used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing and terms of assets used or scraped
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you mention the license of the assets? If you scraped data from a particular source (e.g., Twitter), you should state the copyright and terms of service of that source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State licenses and any relevant copyright/terms for sources; check curated resources (e.g., paperswithcode.com's licensing guide) when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release of new assets (license and terms)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are releasing assets, you should include a license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear licensing and terms for any released code, data, or models to enable reuse and clarify restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repackaged dataset licensing disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are repackaging an existing dataset, you should state the original license as well as the one for the derived asset (if it has changed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make provenance and any license changes explicit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anonymization of assets for initial review
rubrics_metrics.description: For initial review, anonymize your assets. You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When including code/data during anonymous submission, ensure the assets do not reveal author identity. If you cannot release assets, state why (e.g., proprietary information).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent and data provenance
rubrics_metrics.description: Where possible, discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose data you're using/curating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document consent procedures and provenance for datasets derived from people.

rubrics_metrics.name: PII and offensive content disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you discuss whether the data you are using/curating contains personally identifiable information or offensive content?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage discussion of potentially undesirable properties; note offensive material may target vulnerable populations and refer to the Code of Conduct when selecting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid targeting vulnerable populations with offensive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Offensive material (as data) in your manuscript may target specific vulnerable populations, and a reviewer may be a member of that population.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the Code of Conduct when selecting materials for inclusion to avoid targeting; be cautious including offensive examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation for crowdsourcing/human-subjects (instructions and consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you used crowdsourcing or conducted research with human subjects: Did you include the instructions given to participants including the consent form?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the exact instructions and consent materials in supplemental materials where possible (anonymized during review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant risk description
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe any potential participant risks?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include risks from exposing participants to offensive content or collecting PII; explicitly describe foreseeable risks.

rubrics_metrics.name: IRB approval disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. For initial submissions, do not include information that would break anonymity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare IRB approval without revealing identifying details that would compromise the anonymous review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant compensation reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the estimated hourly wage paid to participants and the total amount spent on participant compensation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report payment rates and total compensation to support reproducibility and ethical assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accurate main claims in abstract/introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper's contributions and scope?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are neither overstated nor misleading; align abstract/intro with actual results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you describe the limitations of your work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly discuss limitations and scope; refer to FAccT 2022 guidance for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of theoretical assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are including theoretical results: Did you state the full set of assumptions of all theoretical results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make all assumptions explicit so proofs and results can be properly interpreted and checked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete proofs for theoretical results
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are including theoretical results: Did you include complete proofs of all theoretical results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include full proofs (in paper or supplemental material) to allow verification of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility artifacts for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: If you ran experiments: Did you include the code, data, and instructions needed to reproduce the main experimental results (either in the supplemental material or as a URL, in an anonymized way at the review time)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a README explaining how to reproduce results using provided code; authors are encouraged to release code/data but may state acceptable reasons for not releasing (e.g., proprietary constraints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Training details reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you specify all the training details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report dataset splits, hyperparameter settings, tuning procedures, and selection criteria to enable reproduction and fair comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting of error bars and uncertainty
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you report error bars (e.g., with respect to the random seed after running experiments multiple times)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report variability across runs (e.g., multiple seeds) and include error bars or confidence intervals where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compute and resources disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you include the amount of compute and the type of resources used (e.g., type of GPUs, internal cluster, or cloud provider)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State compute budget, hardware used, and resource providers to contextualize reproducibility and environmental/compute costs.
